summary: Verified the new proxy + WebApp loading strategy. Backend (8/8 pytest) — proxy returns 200 with <base> tag and JS shim ('astra-proxy', XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open, window.fetch) injected for example.com / DuckDuckGo / Hacker News (>=3 wrapped URLs) / MDN / GitHub; Wikipedia returns the friendly bot-block landing page (200 with 'blocked the proxy' + 'Open in real browser' + original URL); CSS rewriting (Google Fonts) returns text/css with url("/api/proxy?url=...") rewrites. Frontend Playwright (8/8) — registered fresh user, installed HN/DDG/Discord from Store via desktop-icon-Store, then desktop-app-hn loads with direct src (https://news.ycombinator.com), desktop-app-ddg loads with proxy src (/api/proxy?url=https%3A%2F%2Fduckduckgo.com), .ax-webapp-bar count = 0 (chrome-less), overlay reveals reload/togglemode/extopen buttons, togglemode swaps src from proxied to direct, Discord renders webapp-discord-fallback with no iframe.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1039 lines (proxy + auth + chat + admin in one file). The proxy block alone is ~330 lines and worth its own module/router (e.g. backend/proxy.py with /api/proxy + helpers).

/api/proxy still accepts arbitrary URLs without auth — same SSRF/abuse risk flagged in iteration_1. Should at minimum (a) require Bearer token, (b) block private/loopback/link-local IPs after DNS resolution, (c) cap response size.

JS shim replaces window.WebSocket with a function whose .prototype is assigned AFTER construction — this still throws on `new WebSocket(...)` (intended) but breaks code that does `WebSocket.OPEN` constant access. Minor; could expose the original constants for compatibility.
_rewrite_html regexes don't handle attributes split across lines or with single quotes inside double quotes (e.g. action="foo'bar"). Rare but worth a comment.

The bot-block heuristic uses `len(body) < 1500` for 401/403/429 — Wikipedia's 403 happens to be ~1.1KB so it works, but a larger custom 403 page would skip the friendly branch. Consider always wrapping 401/403/429 regardless of size.

is_blocked second branch triggers on `len(body) < 800` AND 'cloudflare'/'robot policy'/'access denied' — but on a successful response that's < 800 bytes and happens to contain the word 'cloudflare' (e.g. a CDN-served small fragment) it would also trigger. Tighten by also gating on status_code != 200.
